title: Incremental North Star sprint log — Rahul Patel
content:
Purpose: personal, hypothesis-driven log for moving the 'inference reliability' north-star metric via small, testable bets. This is my working journal — messy, incremental, meant for quick iteration and asynchronous handoffs.

90-day North Star objective (owner: Rahul): Improve production tail-latency reliability (p99 request success with <2s tail) for hosted small-model text generation customers while keeping token cost delta <= +5%.

Key Results (KR) - baseline -> target -> rough progress:
- KR1: p99 success latency for standard text gen route: 3.8s -> 2.0s (baseline Jan-05: 3.8s). Progress: 35% (fast-path routing spike reduction rolling).
- KR2: Average per-token infra cost change versus baseline: 0% -> <= +5%. Progress: 60% (quantization + batching configs saving offsetting some changes).
- KR3: On-call rate for latency incidents per week: 2.1 -> <=0.5. Progress: 20% (early detection hooks added, fewer surprises).

Working hypotheses (short):
H1: A small routing rule that prefers warm KV-cache hosts for <256 token requests will reduce tail retries by 20-30% without hurting cost significantly. Acceptance: measurable p99 improvement in a canary group over 2 weeks, token-cost delta < +5%.
H2: Enabling 4-bit quantization for a narrow set of low-sensitivity models reduces mean token CPU time by ~18% and is transparent to quality for our eval prompt set. Acceptance: embedding cosine/quality drift <0.5% and cost reduction >= 12%.
H3: Adding a lightweight pre-check (fast synthetic token budget estimator) can prevent large requests from being routed to low-memory nodes, reducing OOM fallbacks. Acceptance: fewer OOM fallbacks in canary and no extra latency for normal requests.

Planned micro-experiments (next 3 sprints):
- Sprint A (Jan 06–Jan 20): Implement routing preference flag (canary=10%) + observability tags. Measure p50/p95/p99 and retry counts per route. Linked jira ENG-2145. Owner: Rahul.
- Sprint B (Jan 21–Feb 04): Small-scope quantization toggle for 2 models, run A/B with offline eval set; surface quality deltas in dashboard. Owner: Sophie.
- Sprint C (Feb 05–Feb 25): Add pre-check in proxy layer, run on staging, then 5% canary. Owner: Eliot.

Recent sprint notes (chronological):
- 2026-01-07: Kickoff for routing flag. Quick dev spike showed instrumentation gap (no route-level retry tag for some legacy routes). Added TODOs to ENG-2172.
- 2026-01-15: Canary rollout (10%) for routing flag. Early signal: p95 improved ~8%, p99 not yet moved. Need to increase canary or expand metric windows.
- 2026-01-28: Discovered edge-case where burstily cold cache workloads cause a host to be marked unhealthy and we cascade retries. Hypothesis: health checks too sensitive for cache-populating traffic. Filed follow-up notes.
- 2026-02-12: Quantization toggle integrated into model config; initial offline eval shows 0.3% average perplexity change, quality ok on most prompts. Need more adversarial prompts.
- 2026-03-02: Small drop in incidents after improved tracing; still seeing two tail incidents tied to a particular region under high-concurrency.

Personal work cadence & constraints:
- Deep work: block M/W/F 9:00–12:00 for code + metrics. Avoid meetings then where possible.
- Energy: afternoons are lower bandwidth; prefer async reviews 14:00–17:00.
- Time budget: ~60% engineering hands-on, 20% metrics/observability, 20% coordination/documentation.

Blockers and open questions:
- Need an SRE review on health-check sensitivity change before widening routing canary (owner: SRE).
- Legal/compliance check for quantized model variants for customers on Dedicated (privacy implications?). Pinged security slack #sec-compliance.
- Observability: need a single dashboard that links per-route p99, retry count, and cost delta over time (raised as backlog request in product-ops).

Action items (next 7 days):
- Finish unit + integration tests for routing preference flag (Rahul).
- Add a synthetic load test that emulates cold-cache bursts (Eliot).
- Draft short note for Product on risk/rollback plan for quantization canary (Sophie).
- Schedule SRE sync and attach runbook to ENG-2172.

Retrospective (mini):
What worked: small canaries + focused metrics made it possible to detect signal without wide blast radius.
What didn't: we under-instrumented route meta-tags earlier — lost early signal for one regression.
Next improvements: require route-level tags in every deployment (pre-commit lint?), expand canary duration for p99-sensitive experiments.

Notes to self (random):
- Keep PR titles explicit: "canary: routing-preference -> add route-tag". Easier to filter.
- Tag everything with ENG ticket for traceability.
- If p99 doesn't budge after routing + quantization, consider a small-model fallback with CPU-optimized kernel.

Quick wins I can do today:
- Add missing retry tag to legacy routes (10–30m).
- Push a tiny observability shim to probe count of cache-warm hosts per minute (30m).

Mood + energy: motivated but cautious. Need to be more ruthless about dropping low-signal experiments.

If someone reads this and wants context: see ENG-2145, PR #832, and the short confluence note (linked above).
